sources.provider: U.S. Department of Commerce / NIST CHIPS for America

facts: NIST's CHIPS award record states that the U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Texas Instruments up to $1.61 billion in direct funding to support more than $18 billion of TI investment through the end of the decade for three new fabrication facilities in Texas and Utah.

The NIST record identifies two Sherman, Texas 300-mm fabs targeting 65nm-130nm analog and embedded processing semiconductors and a Lehi, Utah 300-mm fab targeting 28nm-65nm analog and embedded processing semiconductors.

The government record states that the projects are intended to strengthen domestic supply-chain resilience and current-generation/mature-node semiconductor capacity and estimates more than 2,000 manufacturing jobs plus over 20,000 construction jobs over time.
risks: Government support and planned capacity do not establish fab utilization, realized return on invested capital, current valuation, or demand durability; those remain Alpha underwriting questions.
unknowns: Current utilization and incremental returns on the new 300-mm capacity are not established by this award record.
Current market valuation and peer-relative economics remain outside this Scout assist.
